title: 10-Year TIPS auction (second reopening of CUSIP 91282CRE3) — real-yield supply, sized by the 11-12 announcement
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF (home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/Tentative-Auction-Schedule.pdf), fetched direct by plain curl 2026-09-08 (HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes) and its text layer decompressed stream-by-stream. Row reads verbatim `10-Year TIPS R T / Announcement Thursday, November 12, 2026 / Auction Thursday, November 19, 2026 / Settlement Monday, November 30, 2026`, where Treasury's trailing `R` marks a reopening and `T` marks TIPS. 1:00pm ET is Treasury's standing convention and is NOT separately sourced. Filed estimate on the two limits this lane records: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: DISCOVERED during the treasury-coupon-announcement-2026-11-12 initial research (2026-09-08). It is the second of the two auctions that announcement exists to size. PREDICTED CUSIP 91282CRE3, term `9-Year 8-Month` — an inference from a cycle, not a fetched field: treasurydirect's upcoming feed does not reach November yet. The cycle is clean on the record (fiscaldata auctions_query filtered on `inflation_index_security: Yes`, pulled 2026-09-08, n=44): every July 10Y TIPS new issue since 2023 has been reopened exactly twice, in September and November — 91282CHP9 (2023-07-20) reopened 09-21 and 11-21, 91282CLE9 (2024-07-18) reopened 09-19 and 11-21, 91282CNS6 (2025-07-24) reopened 09-18 and 11-20. 91282CRE3 sold as a $21B new issue 2026-07-23 and its first reopening is treasury-10y-tips-2026-09-17, already tracked. EXPECTED SIZE $19B, supported twice over and INDEPENDENTLY of any published guidance: reopenings print exactly $2B below their own CUSIP's new issue in 14 of 14 cases across 8 CUSIPs and 4 years, and the second reopening has equalled the first in 7 of 7 CUSIP pairs. THE ASYMMETRY WORTH RECORDING: sb0590's TIPS FINANCING paragraph covers only the August-to-October quarter, so this size is genuinely unpublished — but a TIPS size change has NEVER expressed at a reopening in the observed window. Every step in the series (17 -> 18 -> 19 -> 20 -> 21) landed on a NEW ISSUE, i.e. the January and July slots, and the ratchet has in any case been flat for three consecutive new issues (2025-07, 2026-01, 2026-07 all $21B) and five consecutive reopenings ($19B). So even a TIPS increase announced at the 2026-11-04 refunding would structurally express at the January 2027 new issue rather than here. Proposed as an estimate; symbols: [] and no house playbook is rates-keyed, so nothing here licenses an entry.
